outputs.L1: We present an algorithm that generates the complete classification of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for any given dimension \(d\). The algorithm takes a single input: the positive integer \(d\). It has been used to classify smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for \(d \leq 7\), yielding 7,622 isomorphism classes in dimension 6 and 72,256 isomorphism classes in dimension 7.
outputs.L2: We introduce a procedure that, given only a positive integer \(d\), enumerates all smooth Fano polytopes of dimension \(d\) up to isomorphism. This method has been applied in dimensions \(d \leq 7\), yielding 7,622 isomorphism classes in dimension 6 and 72,256 in dimension 7.
outputs.L3: The algorithm produces a complete classification of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes for any specified dimension \(d\). Its only input is a positive integer \(d\), representing the desired dimension. It has been successfully applied to classify smooth Fano polytopes in all dimensions \(d \leq 7\). In particular, the classification contains 7,622 isomorphism classes of smooth Fano 6-polytopes and 72,256 isomorphism classes of smooth Fano 7-polytopes.
outputs.L4:
We present an algorithm that, for any positive integer \(d\), generates a complete classification of smooth Fano \(d\)-dimensional lattice polytopes up to lattice isomorphism. The method systematically constructs all possible candidates, tests the smoothness and Fano conditions, and eliminates isomorphic duplicates, thereby producing an exhaustive classification list. Through the standard correspondence between smooth Fano polytopes and smooth toric Fano varieties, the resulting lists also classify smooth toric Fano varieties in the corresponding dimensions.

An implementation of the algorithm was used to carry out the classification through dimension \(7\). It yields \(7{,}622\) isomorphism classes of smooth Fano polytopes in dimension \(6\) and \(72{,}256\) classes in dimension \(7\). Together with the previously known results in lower dimensions, these computations complete the classification of smooth Fano polytopes—and hence of smooth toric Fano varieties—for every dimension \(d\leq 7\).

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main result of a paper on an algorithm for classifying smooth Fano polytopes, including the known counts in dimensions 6 and 7.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper develops a finite, implementable algorithm that classifies smooth Fano polytopes up to unimodular lattice equivalence. It uses a distinguished “special facet” to bound and systematically enumerate possible vertices, while pruning partial configurations that cannot form a smooth Fano polytope.

Applying the algorithm gives complete classifications of:

- **Dimension 6:** **7,622** isomorphism classes  
- **Dimension 7:** **72,256** isomorphism classes

Thus, the main result is both a general classification procedure in any fixed dimension and the first complete enumerations in dimensions 6 and 7.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise research abstract describing an algorithm that takes a positive integer \(d\) and outputs all smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes up to isomorphism.
counterfactuals.output: We present a finite algorithm for classifying smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes up to lattice isomorphism. The method exploits the existence of a distinguished facet whose vertices form a lattice basis and induce sharp bounds on the coordinates and combinatorial positions of all remaining vertices. After normalizing this facet to the standard basis, the algorithm recursively enumerates admissible vertex sets, pruning candidates that violate convexity, smoothness, or the condition that the origin lie strictly in the interior. Each completed polytope is converted to a canonical lattice normal form, allowing isomorphic duplicates to be removed. The coordinate bounds guarantee termination, while the distinguished-facet argument proves that every smooth Fano \(d\)-polytope occurs in the search. Thus, for any positive integer \(d\), the algorithm outputs exactly one representative of every isomorphism class of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Briefly explain the classification algorithm for smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes and state up to which dimension it has been applied.
counterfactuals.output:
Øbro’s algorithm uses the fact that every smooth Fano \(d\)-polytope has a **special facet**. After a unimodular change of coordinates, this facet can be taken to have vertices \(e_1,\ldots,e_d\). Bounds derived from the special-facet condition restrict all other vertices to a finite set of lattice points. The algorithm then builds possible vertex sets recursively, pruning candidates that violate convexity, the Fano condition, facet smoothness, or lattice-isomorphism tests.

This method has produced the complete classification of smooth Fano polytopes **through dimension \(8\)**.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a short mathematical summary of the complete classification of smooth Fano polytopes for \(d \leq 7\), mentioning the algorithm’s input and the enumeration results.
counterfactuals.output:
A **smooth Fano \(d\)-polytope** is a full-dimensional lattice polytope \(P\subset \mathbb{R}^d\) containing \(0\) in its interior such that the vertices of every facet form a \(\mathbb Z^d\)-basis.  

Øbro’s enumeration algorithm takes the dimension \(d\) as input, fixes a “special facet” up to \(\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb Z)\), and recursively constructs all admissible vertex sets, outputting one representative of each unimodular-equivalence class.

For \(1\le d\le 7\), the numbers of smooth Fano \(d\)-polytopes are
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
d&1&2&3&4&5&6&7\\ \hline
\#&1&5&18&124&866&7622&72256.
\end{array}
\]
Thus there are \(80\,892\) equivalence classes in total through dimension \(7\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
